oracle.cross_check: scipy==1.18.1 scipy.stats.entropy: sum_y p(y)[H(G)-H(G|y)] agreed with dit's I(G;Y) to 1e-13 on every case
oracle.algorithm: I(G;Y) = sum_g p(g) sum_y p(y|g,d) [H(G)-H(G|y,d)] on the joint law of graph and observation
asserted_outputs: exact expected information gain per candidate case, compared with product scores at score_atol
candidate ordering and monotonicity in design amount
context_only_outputs: reliability and prior_entropy are retained inputs/context, not product outputs

reference_review.scope: Six fixed candidate cases on one three-graph posterior: mutual information I(G;Y) of the joint law of graph and a symmetric-noise observation channel at the recorded reliabilities. Regeneration reproduces the frozen values at absolute 1e-12 from the declared posterior and reliabilities only.
reference_review.independence_basis: The retained script constructs the joint law from the declared weights, feature labels and reliability and evaluates it with the public dit.shannon.mutual_information API, then cross-checks against the direct definition with scipy.stats.entropy (the two must agree to 1e-12 before any comparison). It imports no Antecedent code. The map from a candidate's amount to its reliability is a recorded input, not recomputed here, so the product's reliability formula is not independently verified by this fixture.
reference_review.historical_exposure: The original harness was deleted; its authorship and exposure cannot be reconstructed beyond the retained digest and environment note (preserved in historical_oracle). The replacement was written from the fixture's normalization statement and the public dit API; no dit source or tests were consulted.
reference_review.redistribution: Repository-authored MIT OR Apache-2.0 script and deterministic inputs. dit (BSD-3-Clause), NumPy and SciPy are tooling dependencies in an isolated locked script environment, outside the product and ordinary CI; no upstream source is stored.
reference_review.limitations: One posterior (3 graphs, 3 categories), symmetric uniform-noise channel, discrete exact information gain only. Sampling-based objectives, non-uniform noise, continuous observations and the amount-to-reliability mapping are outside this reference. The product assertion compares Monte Carlo/exact scores at score_atol 0.006, not at the reference's 1e-12 regeneration tolerance. Calibration remains deferred.

normalization.observation_channel: p(y|g) = reliability*1[y = feature(g)] + (1-reliability)/category_count; reliability 0 is uninformative, 1 is perfect
normalization.information_gain: expectation is taken before any non-negativity check; individual entropy reductions are not clipped
